Content Length Guide

Ideal Word Counts for Every Format

Use these benchmarks to optimise your content for SEO, social media, and engagement.

SEO Blog Post

1,500–2,500 words

Google tends to rank longer, comprehensive articles higher for competitive keywords. Aim for 1,500+ words minimum and cover the topic thoroughly.

Meta Title

50–60 characters

Google displays roughly 60 characters before cutting off with "...". Put your keyword at the start and keep it under 60 chars for best display.

Meta Description

120–160 characters

Descriptions longer than 160 characters get truncated. Write a compelling summary with a call to action to improve click-through rates.

Tweet / X Post

71–100 characters

Shorter tweets under 100 characters get more engagement. Leave room for retweets by keeping it under 250 characters even with the 280 limit.

LinkedIn Post

1,300–2,000 chars

LinkedIn shows "see more" after about 200 characters. Hook readers in the first two lines. Longer posts (1,000–3,000 chars) get more engagement on LinkedIn.

Email Subject Line

40–50 characters

Most email clients show 40–50 characters before cutting off, especially on mobile. Put the most important word first and avoid spam trigger words.

Word Count FAQ

Common Questions

How many words should a blog post be for SEO?+

For competitive keywords, aim for 1,500–2,500 words. Google consistently ranks longer, more comprehensive content higher. That said, quality matters more than length — a focused 1,000-word article beats a padded 3,000-word one. Use this tool to track your word count as you write.

How long does it take to read 1,000 words?+

The average adult reads 200–250 words per minute, so 1,000 words takes about 4–5 minutes to read. This tool calculates reading time at 200 wpm. For speaking (e.g. presentations or videos), use 150 wpm — 1,000 words takes about 6–7 minutes to say.

What counts as a word?+

Any sequence of characters separated by a space counts as one word. Numbers, hyphenated words, and contractions each count as one word. This matches the standard used by Microsoft Word and Google Docs.

What is keyword density and what should it be?+

Keyword density is the percentage of times a word appears relative to total word count. For SEO, there's no magic number — Google uses context, not keyword stuffing. A density of 1–2% for your primary keyword is natural. Focus on covering the topic thoroughly rather than hitting a specific density.

Does this tool save or store my text?+

No. This tool runs entirely in your browser. Your text is never sent to any server, never stored, and never shared. When you close the tab or clear the text, it's gone. Feel free to paste confidential content.
